acceptance: `evolve ship --class manual --force-with-lease` on a diverged feature-branch fixture pushes with the lease (red: flag provided but not defined)
On main, or with --class cycle, it exits 1 and pushes nothing
A remote that moved after ship observed it fails the lease, and ship reports it
fix: Add `--force-with-lease` to `evolve ship --class manual`. It pushes with --force-with-lease=<branch>:<the remote SHA ship observed>, and only when the current branch is not main and not in the protected-branch list from policy config. The cycle and release classes never accept it. A refusal exits 1 naming the rule. Document it in runtime-reference.md's ship classes.
source: console, 2026-09-30, core-function CLI inventory (operator request: a CLI request for each core function)
summary: The ship guard denies raw `git push` (internal/guards/ship.go:22), and ship's push and repair ladder never force-push (internal/phases/ship/landing/push.go:111). When a console branch is amended or rebased after its first push (a review fix, a rebase onto main), `evolve ship --class manual` is rejected as diverged. The only way forward is `git push --force-with-lease` under a guard bypass, which also switches the guard off for anything else in that command.
title: Re-shipping a diverged feature branch needs a raw force push under a guard bypass; add `--force-with-lease` to the manual ship (lane part)
